greet.text: Ah, a pair of legs. Magister Aurel, of the Collegium's Tide College, temporarily of Maren's back room. I'm supposed to be measuring the stones by night, and my knees have voted against it. Would you take some readings for me? Three nights, at the circle. I pay.

choices.text: The Tide College. Do you teach?

greet_scholar.text: You'll be the one they sent with the letter. Good. Magister Aurel, Tide College; I've been here a week and my knees have resigned. Three readings at the stones, three separate nights. Then we write it up and the Collegium ignores it, as is traditional.

choices.text: The Tide College. Do you teach?

what.text: Whether the stones' power is moving. It shouldn't be. Old circles hold their power like a well holds water: still. If the needle in this glass points anywhere, something is drawing on them.

give.text: Splendid. Hold it up near the stones after dark, once a night. Don't drop it; it's older than both of us put together.

waiting.text: Any luck with the readings? Three nights, remember; the stones don't care how impatient we are.

choices.text: The Tide College. Do you teach?

lost.text: Lost the... Fine. I have a spare, because I know myself. Try not to lose this one.

report.text: Well? What did the needle say?

choices.text: North. Every night, steadier. On the last night it didn't move at all.

report_north.text: He goes very quiet. "Drawn north, steadily. Like a river." He writes for a long time. "The Collegium will want this. Or rather, someone at the Collegium will want it buried, and I'd very much like to know who." He counts out your pay.

choices.text: (Scholar) Send it to the Collegium anyway.

report_scholar.text: Oh, I will. Under both our names. If someone buries it, at least we'll know whose shovel it was.

done.text: I've written to three people at the Collegium. Two haven't answered. Interesting, isn't it?

choices.text: The Tide College. Do you teach?

sees_stain.text: Aurel looks at you over his spectacles for slightly too long. "Your pupils don't shrink in the lamplight. The Collegium has a word for that, and it isn't a polite one." He writes something down. "Whatever you've been drinking, stop. And don't tell anyone in a robe."

teach.text: To anyone who pays, which the College finds vulgar and I find necessary. Tidecraft: the pull of the moons. Pull a thing to you, shove it away, open a well and hold it down. Mind the sky: it's strongest when Ilun is full or the Wanderer is dark, and feeble when Ilun is dark and the Wanderer bright. Plan your fights by the moons, as sailors do.

sold_pull.text: He hands over a thin primer, its margins full of moon tables. "Read it twice. The first time you'll pull your own boots off."

sold_shove.text: "Push from the stomach, not the hand. And never in a library." He sounds like he speaks from experience.

sold_well.text: "For the one who walked to those stones three nights running. A well holds whatever falls into it. Don't stand in your own."

well_later.text: "The well is the deep end. I teach it to people who've done the College a favour. Three nights at the stones, say." He taps the rune-glass case meaningfully.

why_moons.text: "Every tide in the world answers them. The sea, the sap, the blood in your ears. The College says the moons are only stones in the sky and we measure their weight." He hesitates. "The Wanderer pulls harder than a stone that size should. Nobody at the College likes that question."

sold_crush.text: He lowers his voice. "The deep end of the deep end. The College calls it Moon-Crush; the sailors call it the Weight. Don't cast it over your own feet, and never indoors under anything you'd miss."

crush_later.text: "Learn to open a well first. Holding a weight comes before dropping one."
